svg.text: — an unconstrained history expert and a structural expert, normalised separately and mixed into one exact distribution

g.text: all facts with t′ < t · optional
o′ is more frequent and more recent than o★: every monotone scorer ranks it higher

svg.text: not monotone in Δt · outside Prop. 1

g.text: no monotone scorer ranks o★ above o′

svg.text: S: past objects of (s, r), of s, and top objects of r

g.text: ranks only what structure alone can score
S candidates compete only with each other
P(o | q) = π·pS(o) [o ∈ S] + (1 − π)·pN(o) [o ∉ S]
trained by −log P(o★ | q) · a single softmax over all N is the special case it generalises
Why separate normalisation: one softmax over all N must order the ≤256 historical candidates among themselves and, with the same logits, against thousands
of entities without history. Two normalisations remove that coupling (+0.37 MRR on WIKI, +0.67 on ICEWS18 over a shared softmax, three seeds), whatever the form of π.
